description:
Follow-up to cross-surface-baseline-update-flag (#935), which shipped the manual
`--update-baseline` maintenance affordance (a YAML baseline in
cross_surface_baseline.yaml, pruned by known_divergences_baseline.py via the
`make cross-surface-update-baseline` target). That item deferred the automation:
detection and pruning are still operator-initiated, so a resolved (no-longer-
reproducing) known-divergence entry can linger between manual sweeps.

Add a scheduled job that runs the enforced cross-surface gates, detects resolved
entries (the gate already reports "previously-known divergences now equivalent"),
runs the existing `--update-baseline` writer, and opens a PR with the pruned
baseline. Removal stays explicit and reviewable (a PR), never a side effect of a
blocking gate run.

anti_patterns.why: soundness path, Code Owner review required.

anti_patterns.dont: reimplement the pruning logic; invoke the #935 writer/target.

preserves.behavior: A still-reproducing divergence is never removed; only resolved entries are dropped; idempotent.
The blocking gate run never prunes; pruning happens only in the scheduled PR path (as #935 established).

prior_art.concept: {'ref': '.github/workflows/release-canary.yml', 'note': 'Existing scheduled-workflow + RULESET_DRIFT_TOKEN pattern to model the cadence and bot-PR mechanics on.'}
{'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py (run_gate resolved-key reporting)', 'note': 'The gate already computes resolved keys; the scheduler reads them rather than re-deriving.'}

{'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/known_divergences_baseline.py + Makefile cross-surface-update-baseline', 'note': 'The load/prune/dump writer and Make target shipped by #935; the scheduled job invokes these, does not reimplement pruning.'}

verifications.command: seed a resolved entry, run the detection step -> it identifies exactly that entry and the writer's diff drops only it
verifications.description: Dry-run detects a seeded resolved entry and produces the expected prune diff
verifications.expected: resolved entry surfaced and pruned; no live entry touched; no-op when none resolved

work_units.evidence: Added _project/scripts/cross_surface_baseline_autodetect.py: phase 1 (detect_and_prune) calls run_gate(gate, update_baseline=False) - byte-identical to the blocking CI call - and parses (never recomputes) the printed 'GATE FAILURE - previously-known divergences now equivalent: [...]' line via regex+ast.literal_eval. run_autodetect() iterates sorted(cross_surface.GATES), the live enforced-gate registry. Verified against the real ssb gate (uv run -- python _project/scripts/cross_surface_baseline_autodetect.py --gates ssb): 31s, exit clean, no-op JSON output, baseline file untouched.
work_units.notes:
A scheduled workflow (or an extension of an existing canary) that runs each
enforced gate and captures the resolved-entry report. No-op when nothing
resolved.
work_units.summary: Scheduled job runs the enforced gates and collects resolved baseline entries per gate

work_units.evidence: Phase 2 of detect_and_prune (same script) runs ONLY when phase 1 named a resolved key, and invokes run_gate(gate, update_baseline=True) - the exact --update-baseline/'make cross-surface-update-baseline' code path from #935 (known_divergences_baseline.update_baseline_file); no pruning logic reimplemented. Added .github/workflows/cross-surface-baseline-autodetect.yml (weekly Sun 10:00 UTC + workflow_dispatch): runs the script, diffs cross_surface_baseline.yaml, and if changed opens/updates a PR against develop via a chore/cross-surface-baseline-autoprune branch (bot-PR mechanics modeled on seed-corpus.yml/todo-db-export.yml: benchbox-bot commit identity, optional CROSS_SURFACE_BASELINE_PR_TOKEN falling back to github.token so pr.yml can still fire for CI signal). NO-OP (no commit/PR) when nothing resolved, per the writer's own idempotent behavior. Added 'make cross-surface-baseline-autodetect' as the local dry-run entry point (Makefile ~line 260).
work_units.notes:
Invoke `make cross-surface-update-baseline BENCHMARK=<gate>` for each affected
gate, then open a bot-authored, labeled PR with the pruned cross_surface_
baseline.yaml. Idempotent: no PR when nothing changed.
work_units.summary: When resolved entries exist, run --update-baseline and open a PR with the pruned baseline

work_units.evidence: Guardrails: (1) never-auto-merge - the workflow never calls gh pr merge --auto anywhere, and separately benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface_baseline.yaml is already a soundness path in _project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py/.github/CODEOWNERS, so the repo-wide auto-merge-on-open.yml backstop independently refuses auto-merge for this PR's diff regardless of authoring token - defense in depth, documented in the workflow header. (2) blocking-gate-never-prunes - pr.yml's correctness-gate job and every 'make <gate>-cross-surface-equivalence-report' Make target are UNMODIFIED (only run_gate(update_baseline=False)); only the new scheduled workflow ever passes update_baseline=True. (3) idempotence - update_baseline_file only writes on an actual diff (verified by test_detect_and_prune_is_a_no_op_once_the_baseline_is_already_clean: byte-identical file, writer never invoked, when nothing is resolved). (4) still-reproducing entries never dropped - verified by test_detect_and_prune_surfaces_exactly_the_resolved_entry_and_prunes_only_it and test_still_reproducing_divergence_alone_is_never_treated_as_resolved.
work_units.notes:
cross_surface.py / the baseline are CODEOWNERS soundness paths, so the prune PR
must leave auto-merge OFF and route to Code Owner review (reuse
auto_merge_soundness_paths.py).
work_units.summary: Guardrails: never auto-merge the prune PR; it touches a soundness path
